authoritative_findings: IRDAI defines indemnity-based and benefit-based Health insurance as distinct regulatory product categories.
IRDAI product-filing/performance reporting formats require product name, UIN and Line of Business with values including Health-Indemnity and Health-Benefit Based.
Therefore benefit_basis is not inherently a semantic-only fact and strict blind selection has not reached a structural ceiling on this predicate.
The public Health Insurance Products register does not expose benefit_basis as a consistently available structured field.

No publicly acquirable regulator or insurer metadata surface was demonstrated in this review that exposes benefit_basis for arbitrary candidate products while remaining structurally bounded before selector exposure.

allowed: regulator return/report metadata keyed by product and UIN
insurer structured product metadata record whose fields are bounded before selector exposure
structurally isolated filing cover sheet containing only approved classification metadata
forbidden: semantic-bearing filed product document filtered after parsing
product marketing copy or FAQ used as semantic inference

reason_structural_ceiling_not_proven: The regulator itself requires benefit-basis classification as structured product/UIN-linked reporting metadata, proving that the fact can exist outside semantic policy interpretation even though a public bounded acquisition path has not yet been demonstrated.
